question.problem: Let $\mathcal{B}=\{\mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2\}$ and $\mathcal{C}=\{\mathbf{c}_1,\mathbf{c}_2\}$ be bases of $\mathbb{R}^2.$ If $\mathbf{c}_1=\mathbf{b}_2-4\mathbf{b}_1$ and $\mathbf{c}_2=5\mathbf{b}_1+7\mathbf{b}_2,$ find the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{B}}$ from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}.$
question.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $\mathcal{C}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}$ are
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275083/assets/daf4111656a525abf51bf58105831ed11378ed7fc52915e1e58ca5f75884bcf0.svg)

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $\mathcal{C}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}.$
